questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Milan because I wanted to experience Italian culture, food, and everyday life. The city also offers a vibrant international environment with students from all over the world. I was looking for a destination where I could both immerse myself in a new culture and become part of a diverse student community.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was straightforward and flexible. Students can try different courses before deciding which ones to keep and register for through the University of Milan's online system. The platform is intuitive, lecturers are helpful if any questions arise, and there is no pressure, as registration can be completed during the semester before the final exams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors and international office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to look at the course schedule in advance to avoid unnecessary timetable conflicts. I would also recommend trying courses outside your usual field of study, as the flexible registration process makes it easy to explore new and interesting subjects before making your final choices.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Compared to the University of Copenhagen, I found the courses to be less academically demanding. However, there was a greater emphasis on class participation and attendance, with teaching being more discussion-based and interactive. Overall, I found this teaching style engaging and enjoyable.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend simply exploring the city on foot and enjoying the atmosphere of Milan's different neighborhoods, as each has its own unique character. Of course, visiting the Duomo is a must, but some of the best experiences come from wandering the streets, discovering cafés, and enjoying the local culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any major cultural challenges. If anything, I noticed that the pace of everyday life is generally more relaxed, and people tend to be more patient than I was used to. It took a little time to adjust, but I came to appreciate this aspect of Italian culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I appreciated most was the relaxed pace of everyday life and the strong social culture. People spend time together throughout the week, enjoying meals, cafés, and the city rather than only on weekends. I also loved how people made the most of the good weather and the vibrant atmosphere of Milan.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to trying new courses, as the registration process is flexible and allows you to explore different subjects before making your final choices.
Make the most of life outside your studies by exploring Milan's neighborhoods, cafés, and cultural events – the city has much more to offer than its main tourist attractions.
Take every opportunity to meet both local and international students. The exchange community is very welcoming, and it is one of the best parts of the experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was the overall experience. I made great new friendships, had the opportunity to immerse myself in Italian culture, and enjoyed an unforgettable semester filled with both personal and academic growth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any major challenges during my exchange. Naturally, I missed Denmark, my family, and friends from time to time, but it was never overwhelming and was simply a normal part of living abroad.
